newsitem.title: UNITED NATIONS: Iraq-Syria border post to reopen in a month.
newsitem.headline: Iraq-Syria border post to reopen in a month.

text.p: The new border entry point to Iraq from Syria is expected to become operational for goods shipments in about a month, with 10 U.N. inspectors stationed there, the United Nations said on Monday.
U.N. spokesman Fred Eckhard said work was needed on the border post, which had been closed for 10 years until a recent agreement between Iraq and Syria.
"It will take 3 to 4 weeks to become fully operational," said Eckhard. Buildings and roads are in need of repair."
U.N. Secretary-General Kofi Annan approved on Aug. 1 a location on the Iraqi-Syrian border as a new entry point for humanitarian goods to Iraq under the "oil-for-food" plan.
The location is at Al-Walid, opposite Al-Tenf in Syria. Other entry points already in use are the Iraqi port of Umm Qasr, Trebil on the Iraqi-Jordanian border and Zakho on the Iraqi-Turkish border.
The 10 U.N. inspection agents, working on a 24-hour basis, are to be stationed at the newly-designated site to authenticate the arrival of humanitarian supplies.
Under the "oil-for-food" plan Iraq is allowed to export $2 billion worth of oil every six months to help offset the effects of sanctions imposed shortly after its August 1990 invasion of Kuwait.
